title: Development Financial Institutions
definition: Development Financial Institutions (DFIs) are specialized financial intermediaries established to provide long-term risk capital, medium-to-long-term project finance, and advisory services for sectors requiring massive capital outlays with long gestation periods where commercial banks hesitate to lend.
importanceInUpsc: Crucial for GS Paper III (Indian Economy, Infrastructure, Financing Models, Investment); frequently tested in Prelims regarding the difference between commercial banks and DFIs, NABEX/NaBFID structures, and historical evolution of IFCI, IDBI, and ICICI.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Development Financial Institutions.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Core foundational concepts of banking, monetary policy, and infrastructure financing.
